records.name: Greenhouse Heat Demand: Hourly Degree-Hour Balance Calibrated to KEMA 2012
records.evidence_policy: Trusted Source Map and Source Trust Policy for Aquaponics Layer 1; reliability fields per AGENTS.md 6A
records.equation_text: heat_W_per_m2_floor(hour) = max(0, K * f_screen * (T_set - T_out(hour)) - a * I_global(hour)); f_screen = U(glass + thermal blanket)/U(single glass) at night when a screen is used, else 1
structure_assumptions: T_out over the day is a cosine between monthly mean min and max, peaking at 15:00 (assumption, not sourced).
Global radiation is spread over the daylight hours as a half sine; day length from latitude and mid-month solar declination (astronomy).
Day setpoint applies in daylight hours, night setpoint otherwise.
A night screen scales K by U(single glass + thermal blanket)/U(single glass) = 4.0/6.2 (ASABE EP406.4), assuming infiltration falls in proportion (assumption). Day losses are unscreened.
Mean-day normals: cold spells and weather variability are not represented, so peak demand and some annual demand are missed.

calibration.method: K is solved so the model reproduces the KEMA 2012 radish point under De Bilt 1991-2020 normals, once per value of the solar utilisation grid. The data cannot separate K from solar utilisation (the KEMA pot-plant point changes by under 3 percent across the grid), so results are reported as the range across the grid.
calibration.climate_assumption: KEMA modelled a Dutch reference year; De Bilt 1991-2020 normals are assumed close to it (not stated in the source).
calibration.source: KEMA 2012 for Kas als Energiebron, Venlo 2 ha reference greenhouse (catalog candidate greenhouse_heat_demand_m3_aeq_per_m2_year_kema2012)

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: Modelled figures from a consultancy report for the Dutch sector programme, hosted by WUR; not measured.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Stated setpoints and house type; 2012; not herbs; the day/night order of the pot-plant setpoints is read as 15 day / 13 night.

corroboration.note: KEMA 2009 gives radish at the same 12/8 C setpoints about 5.4 m3/m2/yr, less than half of KEMA 2012's 12.0. The difference is not explained in what was read; contradiction ticket drafted in the vault findings note.

point.screen: not stated; treated as no screen

calibration.solar_utilisation_grid_basis: Physical bounds only: 0 (no solar credit) to 1 (all global radiation offsets heat loss). No source gives the value.

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: WUR report; read through a fetch summary only.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Different crop, possible gas-vs-heat basis mismatch, lighting not accounted for.

points.caveat: Same report as the calibration point; tests the screen factor and the setpoint scaling, not independent of KEMA's own model.
points.source: KEMA 2012 for Kas als Energiebron, Venlo 2 ha reference greenhouse (catalog candidate greenhouse_heat_demand_m3_aeq_per_m2_year_kema2012)

points.caveat: 30.8 m3/m2/yr x 31.65 MJ/m3. The source figure may be gas use rather than heat demand, and chrysanthemum is usually lit (lamp heat lowers heat demand); both confound the check. Screen use is assumed.

cover_u_values_w_m2_k.source: ANSI/ASAE EP406.4 JAN03 Table 1 (copy hosted by University of Arizona CEAC); NSW DPI 'Heating greenhouses'; Virginia Tech SPES-821NP Table 1
cover_u_values_w_m2_k.use: Night screen factor (ASABE 4.0/6.2), the K-over-U cross-check and the Karnataka K scaling. Not used to set K directly, because the cover-to-floor ratio is unsourced.

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: ASABE engineering practice standard, corroborated by two government/extension sources.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Double PE agrees across all three (about 4). Single glass and film differ: ASABE 6.2 vs NSW 7 to 8.5, so kept as ranges. Read through fetch summaries.

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: Dutch government definition of the gas equivalent.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Definition, direct; KEMA's 381.5 MJ = 12.0 m3 a.e. matches (31.8 MJ/m3).

gas.boiler_source: Ploeger, van Rijssel, van der Sluis, LEI Rapport 2.99.02 (1999): about 84% without flue-gas condenser, 89 to 92% with one

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Single source, 25+ years old; no current WUR default found.

karnataka_polyhouse.k_scale_basis: Single plastic film vs single glass U: ASABE gives both 6.2 (ratio 1.0); NSW DPI single polythene 7.5 to 8.5 vs glass 3 mm 7.0 to 8.0, high end 8.5/7.0 = 1.21. Geometry and infiltration of a naturally ventilated polyhouse differ from Venlo; not accounted for (gap).
karnataka_polyhouse.heating_practice_note: ICAR Indian Horticulture (Singh et al. 2022, Bundelkhand, not Karnataka): naturally ventilated polyhouses have 'no heating or cooling devices'. NABARD Kerala model project (2015): fan-pad cooling is an optional item.

fan_pad_electricity.basis: Sharan and Madhavan, IIM Ahmedabad working paper 2009-11-04: 120 m2 house, fan-pad 15 to 18 kWh per day, semi-arid North-West India (not Karnataka); surrounding sentence appears to contain a typo

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: Working paper, not peer-reviewed; wrong climate region.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Single source, different region, text possibly garbled; days of operation per year unknown (results assume every day as an upper bound).

gaps: No cover-to-floor area ratio for any house type (K is calibrated instead).
No heat demand for basil or herbs in the Netherlands; basil cases extrapolate K above the 8 to 15 C calibration range.
No U-value for Venlo glass with an energy screen from a Dutch source.
KEMA 2009 vs 2012 radish heat demand disagree by about 2x.
No Bengaluru global radiation; Karnataka heating ignores solar gain (conservative, irrelevant at night).
No Karnataka fan-pad electricity figure and no Karnataka electricity tariff in the catalog.
Water (aquaponics tank) heating, humidity control and ventilation heat loss beyond K are not modelled separately.
Current boiler efficiency figure missing (1999 source).
records.consumers: src/heat_demand.py writes data/simulation/results/greenhouse_heat_demand.json; the configurator (swaps thread) may read heat_demand_m3_aeq_m2_yr and gas_m3_m2_yr from it later.
